QF.id: IV Clearing Settlement and Risk Management_39

question.text: What is the exchange-level overall open position limit on all interest rate derivative (IRD) contracts on a specific underlying bond?

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook caps the exchange-level overall open position on all IRD contracts on a specific underlying at 25% of the outstanding underlying bond. This is an aggregate exchange-level ceiling, distinct from member/client-level open-interest based limits. The Trap: 10%, 15% and 20% are common distractors. In particular, 15% appears in workbook tables for T-Bill/MIBOR trading-member limits as "15% of total open interest or Rs.1000 crore whichever is higher" - which is a different rule on a different base (open interest, not outstanding stock). Note: Page 235 supports the 25% exchange-level cap on outstanding underlying. Individual category (trading member / client) limits are stated separately and are tied to open interest with absolute minimum thresholds.
